Uterine fibroids are benign, non-cancerous growths that develop within or around the muscular walls of the uterus. While many women with fibroids conceive without medical intervention, certain types can influence fertility.

Depending on their size, number, and location, fibroids can:
• Alter the shape of the uterine cavity, impacting embryo implantation.
• Restrict optimal blood circulation to the uterine lining.
• Obstruct the fallopian tubes.

At Embrion IVF Center, we assess each case individually. If a fibroid is affecting your fertility, modern, minimally invasive management can restore optimal uterine health before starting treatment.

If you have faced repeated embryo implantation failure despite transferring high-quality embryos, immune factors within the reproductive tract may be a contributing factor worth investigating.

Natural Killer (NK) cells are a standard, protective component of the body's immune system. However, an imbalance of these cells within the uterine lining can sometimes affect how the body responds to an embryo, impacting its ability to implant safely.

Through advanced reproductive immunological testing, our laboratory can evaluate these cell levels and implement targeted therapeutic options to foster a more receptive environment.

This couple came after two unsuccessful donor IUI cycles, facing challenges on both sides: poor ovarian reserve and zero sperm count.

The outcome: a confirmed clinical pregnancy and the birth of two healthy baby girls.
Every case has a story. The right diagnosis can make all the difference. 💕

A couple with a 7-year history of infertility faced an unexpected hurdle on the day of egg retrieval. While 18 mature eggs were successfully retrieved, no viable sperm was available for fertilisation.

featured_reviews.name: Nishant Mhatre
featured_reviews.review_text:
Our journey toward parenthood was not an easy one and like many couples in Mumbai, we found ourselves surrounded by countless IVF and fertility centres almost one in every locality. However, what truly distinguishes Ankoor Fertility Clinic from the rest is that, unlike many clinics that often feel driven primarily by commercial motives, this institution is driven by passion, integrity and genuine care for patients.

Before visiting Ankoor, my wife and I had already consulted two other gynecologists. Our previous experiences felt largely procedural, where treatments seemed to follow a fixed medical playbook with little effort to understand us as individuals. Meeting Dr. Kedar Ganla was a completely different experience altogether.

What impressed us most was his extraordinary dedication and depth of involvement in understanding every aspect of our lives not just our medical reports. He carefully studied our medical history, lifestyle, dietary habits, stress levels, routines and even patterns that we ourselves had overlooked. His approach was deeply analytical yet profoundly humane.

In many other fertility centres, we felt IVF would have been immediately recommended as the default solution. However, Dr. Kedar Ganla was remarkably honest with us. He explained that even if IVF were attempted immediately, the chances of success would remain low unless we first addressed certain health and lifestyle concerns. More importantly, he reassured us that, in his professional opinion, we did not necessarily require IVF at all. He believed that with disciplined lifestyle changes, proper diet, exercise, weight management, and medication, natural conception was genuinely possible for us.

He gave us clear health goals and monitored our progress rigorously during every consultation. In fact, he often reminded us like a strict yet caring school headmaster about the importance of discipline and consistency. At times he even scolded us for not following instructions properly, but today we realise that his firmness came from sincere concern and commitment toward our success. Sometimes, especially in one’s mid and late thirties, that kind of accountability becomes necessary.

The day we discovered that we had conceived naturally was one of the happiest and most emotional moments of our lives. We immediately remembered Dr. Kedar’s words when he confidently told us, “You will be able to conceive naturally.” and indeed, we did.

That, however, was only the first milestone of our pregnancy journey. There were additional complications and concerns during the pregnancy, many of which we may not fully understand technically even today by us. But throughout the entire journey, we placed complete trust in Dr. Kedar Ganla and Dr. Manjusha Ganla. They, along with their entire team, stood firmly beside us not only until delivery, but even during the post-pregnancy phase with unwavering support and care.

This review is not written for promotion, nor is it generated artificially. It comes from genuine gratitude and heartfelt appreciation. We simply wish to recommend and endorse doctor who practise medicine not merely as a profession, but as a passion and a responsibility toward human life.

We will always remain thankful to Dr. Kedar Ganla, Dr. Manjusha Ganla and the entire team at Ankoor Fertility Clinic for helping us achieve one of the greatest blessings of our lives.

Adenomyosis ≠ IVF for Everyone
Many women believe that a diagnosis of adenomyosis means IVF is the only option—but that's not true.
Treatment depends on several factors, including your age, symptoms, ovarian reserve (AMH), fallopian tube status, semen analysis, and pregnancy goals.
✅ Mild adenomyosis may be managed with medicines, timed intercourse, or IUI.
✅ Moderate cases require individualized treatment and close monitoring.
✅ Severe adenomyosis, low ovarian reserve, failed IUI, or increasing age may make IVF the most effective option. Sometimes, uterine preparation before IVF can further improve the chances of implantation.
The key is early evaluation and a personalized fertility plan. Don't delay seeking expert advice if you're planning a pregnancy.

What is SSG? 🌸

SSG (Saline Sonohysterography) is a special ultrasound test where saline is gently used to clearly see the inside of the uterus.

SSG helps detect:
✅ Uterine polyps
✅ Fibroids
✅ Adhesions or scars
✅ Causes of infertility
✅ Causes of recurrent pregnancy loss

A clear and healthy uterine cavity can improve the chances of implantation and pregnancy. Early diagnosis helps your fertility specialist plan the right treatment at the right time. 💛

At Sunrise Fertility & IVF Centre, we provide accurate fertility evaluation and personalized care for every couple’s parenthood journey.

When Should You Get an HSG Test? 🌸

An HSG (Hysterosalpingography) is a simple X-ray test that checks whether your fallopian tubes are open and evaluates the shape of your uterus. It is an important investigation for couples facing difficulty conceiving.

Your doctor may recommend an HSG if:
✅ You have been trying to conceive for 1 year without success (or 6 months if you are over 35)
✅ Pregnancy is not happening despite regular ovulation
✅ You are planning IUI treatment
✅ There is a suspicion of blocked fallopian tubes or unexplained infertility

Blocked fallopian tubes can prevent the egg and sperm from meeting, making natural conception difficult. Identifying the cause early helps your fertility specialist choose the most appropriate treatment.

💛 Early diagnosis leads to better fertility planning and improved chances of pregnancy.

What is Follicular Study? 🌸

Follicular study is a series of ultrasound scans done to track egg growth and identify the right time of ovulation.

It helps in:
✅ Knowing the exact ovulation day
✅ Tracking follicle/egg growth
✅ Timing intercourse or IUI correctly
✅ Improving chances of pregnancy

Right timing can make all the difference when you are trying to conceive. Follicular study helps identify your most fertile days and supports better fertility planning.

At Sunrise Fertility & IVF Centre, we guide couples with accurate monitoring and personalized fertility care. 💛

What is Unexplained Infertility? 🤔🌸

Unexplained infertility means all common fertility reports may look normal, but pregnancy is still not happening.

Common tests may show normal:
✅ Ovulation
✅ Semen analysis
✅ Fallopian tubes
✅ Hormone levels

But sometimes, the cause may be hidden — like egg quality, sperm function, fertilization issues, implantation problems, or mild endometriosis.

The good news is: treatment options are available. 💛
With expert evaluation, personalized planning, and timely treatment, many couples can still achieve pregnancy.

Don’t lose hope. Consult a fertility specialist and take the next step toward parenthood. ✨
